top_signals.title: Treasury Revamps Debt-Sale Guidance, Holds Auctions Steady
top_signals.summary: The US Treasury revamped the guidance on sales of notes and bonds it has used since early 2024, with new language in the so-called quarterly refunding announcement that may open the door to cuts in the issuance of the longest-dated debt in 2027. Michael McKee reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Corporate America braced for Democrats to unleash investigations
top_signals.summary: Probes could uncover communications between officials and executives after alleged corruption emerged as campaign theme
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: France backs reporting for self-custodied crypto worth 100K euros or more
top_signals.summary: The amendment would require taxpayers to report holdings worth at least $112,000, but the measure still needs to survive the budget process.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Digital asset volatility and institutional crypto positioning changes.

top_signals.title: Government intervenes in Sky’s £1.6bn ITV takeover
top_signals.summary: Culture secretary Lisa Nandy has formally intervened in Sky’s £1.6bn takeover of ITV’s broadcasting business after raising concerns over its impact on media competition and the diversity of British news. Nandy confirmed on Wednesday that she had issued a Public Interest Intervention Notice (PIIN), instructing the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) and media regulator Ofcom [...]
